name: Phase 0 Product Coherence Completion and Phase 1 Handoff
purpose: Freeze NetCoin product identity, information architecture, design-system rules, simplification gates, trust/interaction standards, and no-dead-end workflow rules before proof hardening begins.
north_star: A first-time user understands Core -> Network -> Build -> Ecosystem, with Explorer/Download/Home/Markets/Wallet in Core, in under 30 seconds, while advanced tools remain available through modes, progressive disclosure, and Studio/Network lenses.

completed_layers.locked_decision: Explorer, Download, Home, Markets, and Wallet are the public Core surfaces; secondary systems move under Network, Build, or Ecosystem.
NetCoin uses one page template, one component taxonomy, one status vocabulary, one density system, and one accessibility baseline.
Critical user journeys must follow start -> input -> review -> confirm -> execute -> success -> verify -> recover where appropriate.
New pages are disallowed unless a panel, drawer, settings section, or existing page cannot safely support the workflow.
Every irreversible or high-risk action needs review, trust signals, success reassurance, and failure recovery copy.
Every major surface must have one owner lens, one user job, one primary action, one trust signal, one next step, and one advanced destination.

locked_product_decisions.page_rule: One page, one owner job, one primary action, one trust signal, one next step, one advanced destination.
locked_product_decisions.anti_sprawl_rule: A new feature must improve an existing workflow, remove a hard ceiling, increase trust/safety/clarity, or reduce complexity.
locked_product_decisions.new_surface_rule: Do not create a new top-level surface during Phase 1-5 unless the phase0-complete gate is updated with explicit justification.

phase0_acceptance_criteria: The homepage and top navigation prioritize Wallet, Explorer, and Markets.
Every secondary surface is grouped under Network, Community, or Developers/Studio.
Every major surface maps to exactly one owner job.
Every major surface defines a primary action, trust signal, next step, and advanced destination.
Every critical workflow has a success reassurance and failure recovery path.
The project has a canonical design-system JSON and shared CSS foundation.
The project has a canonical simplification policy that discourages new pages.
The project has a canonical trust/interaction policy for risky actions.
The project has a canonical product coherence policy for no-dead-end pages.
Future features are filtered through anti-sprawl rules before implementation.
Phase 1 can focus on proof hardening instead of product-identity decisions.
Phase 0 validators are wired into a single completion gate.

approved_next_roadmap.name: Proof Hardening
approved_next_roadmap.goal: Prove Python, Rust, TypeScript, API, and browser gates together.

approved_next_roadmap.name: Wallet Professional UX
approved_next_roadmap.goal: Make the wallet the calm home base: security center, review flow, local labels, backup verification, simple/advanced mode.

approved_next_roadmap.name: Explorer and Indexer Trust
approved_next_roadmap.goal: Make chain data trustworthy through active-chain, reorg, pagination, fee-band, and CSV schema improvements.

approved_next_roadmap.name: Markets Risk and Settlement
approved_next_roadmap.goal: Make existing markets safer through order preview, max loss, PnL split, dispute timeline, and settlement explanation.
must_not_add: new market categories before replay and settlement proof

approved_next_roadmap.name: Faucet and Community Hardening
approved_next_roadmap.goal: Add real provider abuse controls, admin audit logs, profile basics, and moderation/bounty lifecycle clarity.
must_not_add: new social mechanics before moderation proof

approved_next_roadmap.name: Exchange and Custody Safety
approved_next_roadmap.goal: Improve existing custody flows with timelines, approvals, reserve explanations, and ledger invariants.
must_not_add: new exchange products before custody proof

approved_next_roadmap.name: Accessibility, Security, and Audit Candidate
approved_next_roadmap.goal: Unify accessibility, fuzz/property tests, signed provenance, and external audit bundle generation.
must_not_add: mainnet launch claims before audit evidence

phase1_handoff.starting_question: Can this version be trusted across Python reference, Rust parity, TypeScript API, browser UI, and release/security gates?
required_evidence: npm ci && npm run ci:api report

definition_of_done: Product identity and navigation are locked.
Design-system, simplification, trust, and coherence contracts exist.
A single Phase 0 completion checker passes.
